answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through verifiable radio multilateration. Each node binds its execution thread to a transceiver exchanging time-stamped pings with anchors across the radio horizon. This forces an adversary to deploy discrete physical hardware at separated locations, such as a cellular tower or coastal jetty, incurring real equipment costs per identity. However, multipath reflections can distort timing delays, causing false rejections of honest nodes.
